sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (investor source jurisdiction; WFOE to be formed in Mainland China)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (PRC civil-statutory law for WFOE formation; Taiwan civil-law system for investor due diligence and corporate documentary authentication)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) between ARATS and SEF
Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Facilitation

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: PRC Company Law (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 7, 10, 23, 24, 32, 46, 47, 49, 59, 60 and 73; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020), Articles 2, 4, 6, 13 and 29; Regulations on the Implementation of the Foreign Investment Law; Administrative Provisions on the Registration of Market Entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and its local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) at the WFOE's registered address; Taiwan-invested entities use the same national SAMR enterprise registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (公司登记申请书), Articles of Association (公司章程), and Foreign Investment Information Report (外商投资信息报告), submitted through the National Enterprise Registration Service Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital for a WFOE limited liability company; capital is subscribed in the Articles of Association and paid into a domestically opened corporate bank account within the shareholder-approved term. No escrow account is mandated under company law; however, local Financial Regulation Bureau practice for commercial factoring companies may require a paid-in capital floor of approximately RMB 5,000,000 before operational licensing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole Shareholder subscribe in full to the registered capital of the Company and adopt the Articles of Association and all formation documents. RESOLVED, that the Company’s registered office shall be [Address], and [City] AMR is designated as the filing authority. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Director and Legal Representative, [Name] is appointed Supervisor, and [Name] is appointed General Manager, each to serve until replaced. RESOLVED, that the Director shall open the capital contribution bank account, execute all registration filings, and apply for the commercial factoring registration and cross-border payment approvals. RESOLVED, that the Company’s fiscal year and accounting standards shall follow PRC law. All actions taken pursuant to these resolutions are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name pre-approval and foreign investment negative-list screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) via National Enterprise Registration Service Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three to five proposed Chinese company names for AMR verification; confirm that the trade-finance factoring scope is not on the foreign investment negative list; obtain the Name Approval Notice before filing the main registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized/certified identity or corporate certificate of the foreign shareholder
Power of attorney for the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit with an adjusted company name and corrected business-scope wording; if the negative-list screening is queried, provide a supplementary legal opinion or obtain a special negative-list approval from NDRC/MOFCOM.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR integrated registration portal; MOFCOM information-reporting system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Foreign Investment Information Report as part of the company registration filing; this is a post-establishment reporting mechanism for non-negative-list industries, not a pre-approval license.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to SAMR/MOFCOM deficiency notice within the stated cure period; amend the Articles of Association or contribution timeline and re-file; use administrative reconsideration if unlawfully rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company incorporation registration and business license issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) at the registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Company Registration Application, Articles of Association, address proof, and legal representative appointment to AMR; upon approval, obtain the Business License (营业执照) with Uniform Social Credit Code.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association executed by all shareholders
Legal representative and supervisor identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct filing mistakes and resubmit; if AMR issues a rejection, file an administrative reconsideration with the next-level SAMR authority or seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal engraving, tax registration, social insurance, and bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (seal filing), State Taxation Administration, and licensed commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Business License, engrave the company seal, legal representative seal, and financial seal; complete tax registration and social insurance enrollment; open a RMB basic deposit account and a foreign currency capital contribution account at a licensed bank.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening application and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-submit any incomplete tax or social security registration; for bank refusal, apply to another licensed bank or escalate to the local branch of the People's Bank of China.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Paid-in capital contribution and foreign exchange registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed domestic bank handling capital contribution; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) registered bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transfer the subscribed capital from the overseas shareholder to the WFOE's capital contribution account; complete foreign exchange receipt and settlement; register the foreign investment capital flow with SAFE where required for cross-border payment rails.
required_dossiers: Business License and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify foreign-exchange discrepancies with the bank and SAFE; obtain an amended investment registration or a bank reconciliation letter; if the capital basis is challenged, execute a supplementary capital contribution agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Financial Regulation Bureau (地方金融监督管理局)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the post-incorporation application for inclusion in the commercial factoring company supervision list; provide the AML/CFT policy, business plans, and qualified management information; obtain the recordal/approval letter before commencing factoring or reverse factoring transactions.
required_dossiers: Internal control and AML/CFT compliance manual
Director and senior management background statements
Factoring business plan and risk management framework
Capital verification or paid-in capital evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the regulator's information request within the statutory cure period; rectify governance or capital deficiencies; if refused, appeal to a higher-level financial regulator or apply for judicial review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA) and local Financial Regulation Bureau; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for cross-border payment rails
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Factoring Company Registration/Recordal Certificate (商业保理公司登记/备案证明) and, where applicable, SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Approval

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the local Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration only; financial-service office premises are normally outside mandatory full EIA requirements, but office fit-out exceeding 50,000 square meters or involving special equipment may require a Registration Form under the 2021 EIA Classification Catalogue.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge for pure factoring operations; where office premises contain data centers or canteens: wastewater must meet GB/T 31962-2015, VOCs/odors must meet GB 37822-2019, and hazardous waste shall be transferred under the five-connection electronic manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire protection acceptance filing (消防验收备案) for the office premises; building structural load certificate from the landlord; occupational health and workplace safety inspection under the Work Safety Law; civil air defense registration or fee where applicable; no physical industrial machinery is installed.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Mainland China: State Taxation Administration (国家税务总局, STA), with provincial and municipal Electronic Tax Bureaus (电子税务局); portal https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn and https://www.chinatax.gov.cn. Taiwan: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (財政部賦稅署), administered locally by the National Taxation Bureaus (國稅局); portal https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw. For the PRC WFOE, the operative registration portal is the STA electronic tax bureau of the jurisdiction where the WFOE is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Chinese WFOE, the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (统一社会信用代码, USCC) on the SAMR business license is the statutory taxpayer identification number under the multi-certificate integration system; no separate tax registration certificate is issued. The WFOE must: (1) complete taxpayer registration in the STA electronic tax bureau within 30 days of business license issuance; (2) verify VAT taxpayer type and elect or apply for general VAT taxpayer status if annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000 or if voluntary classification is beneficial; (3) file banking deposit account information, accounting standards, and legal representative/CFO identification; (4) apply for e-invoice quotas and digital tax certificates; (5) register with the local National Taxation Bureau in Taiwan for an 8-digit Profit-seeking Enterprise Uniform Number (營利事業統一編號) only if a Taiwan fixed place of business or PE is established. In the absence of a Taiwan PE, Taiwan-source factoring fees payable to the WFOE may be subject to Taiwan withholding tax and case-by-case non-resident tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The PRC WFOE is a resident enterprise taxed as a corporation on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Law, and it is a VAT taxpayer in its own right. It is not pass-through and is not eligible for check-the-box flow-through treatment. A Taiwan branch or PE, if any, is subject to Taiwan Profit-seeking Enterprise Income Tax on Taiwan-source income under Taiwan's territorial rules; no special tax-exempt zone status is presumed for the WFOE.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available in Mainland China or Taiwan for a WFOE. In the PRC, the principal statutory elections are: small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment where annual turnover is below RMB 5,000,000, versus voluntary general VAT taxpayer registration; CIT preferential elections such as high-tech enterprise 15% rate, encouraged-industry concession, and accelerated depreciation/amortization. In Taiwan, a Taiwan PE may in limited non-resident cases elect deemed-profits taxation rather than actual-income assessment if books are inadequate, but the WFOE itself cannot elect transparent treatment; hybrid mismatch outcomes are constrained by PRC CFC rules, Taiwan's CFC/Anti-hybrid legislation, and BEPS Action 2, with no standalone taxpayer election to alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (增值税) in Mainland China and Taiwan Value-Added Business Tax under the 加值型及非加值型营业税法. For the WFOE's trade-supply-chain factoring and receivables finance business, PRC VAT applies to factoring commissions and service fees as financial-services VAT; Taiwan Business Tax attaches to services rendered through a Taiwan PE or services used/enjoyed in Taiwan.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: China: every enterprise is required to register for tax/VAT at incorporation irrespective of turnover; there is no zero-turnover de minimis for a juridical person. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration arises once annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; below that threshold, small-scale taxpayer treatment applies (currently a 3% levy with temporary reduced rates as published). Taiwan: a profit-seeking enterprise must register for Business Tax before commencing business, and there is no turnover threshold for company registration; only small-scale sole proprietors may use the simplified registration threshold of monthly taxable sales below NT$300,000, which is not available to a WFOE or corporate branch.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China: mandatory digital e-invoicing through the STA 'fully digitalized electronic invoice' (全面数字化的电子发票) system using XML/OFD format; general VAT taxpayers must issue special VAT invoices through tax-authority-controlled systems with digital signatures and instantaneous transmission to the STA. ERP/API integration or tax-UKey issuance is required in practice; red-letter/negative invoices must be processed through the e-tax platform before the seller may offset output VAT. Taiwan: profit-seeking enterprises must issue statutory Uniform Invoices (統一發票) for Taiwan business receipts, upload e-invoice data to the e-invoice integration service platform (電子發票整合服務平台), and comply with quarterly filing, invoice serial numbering, and digital stamping/QR-code requirements. Taiwan does not operate a full real-time pre-clearance VAT system, but the platform provides near-real-time invoice-data exchange and audit visibility.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A PRC general VAT taxpayer may claim zero-rating and input-VAT refund for physical goods exported from the PRC customs territory if the goods are actually shipped abroad, title passes to a non-resident buyer, export proceeds are collected within the statutory FX repatriation period, and the complete export declaration/invoice/transport/payment chain is evidenced. Cross-border factoring, reverse factoring, and trade-finance services may qualify for zero-rating or VAT exemption only if the services are expressly within the cross-border services catalogue in Caishui 2016 No. 36 and annexes, are consumed entirely outside China, and are provided to an overseas recipient without a PRC establishment; otherwise the services remain taxable at 6%. Taiwan: exported goods and services wholly used or consumed outside Taiwan are zero-rated or exempt from Business Tax when evidenced by export declarations, contracts, invoices, and foreign-exchange receipts.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口货物报关单 / Customs Export Goods Declaration Form)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (B/L or AWB evidencing export shipment)
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Collection Certificate (出口收汇核销)
Export sales contract, commercial invoice, and packing list
VAT special invoice (增值税专用发票) or export invoice evidencing prior input tax
Customs valuation, HS classification, and pricing documentation
Proof of offshore service consumption and non-resident recipient status for cross-border factoring/services, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: China: fraudulent zero-rating or export-refund claims trigger immediate clawback of refunded VAT and disgorgement of input credits, a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, administrative penalties of 50% to five times the tax under Article 63 of the Tax Administration Law, customs fines and confiscation under the Customs Law, and criminal liability for export-tax-refund fraud under Article 204 of the Criminal Law (imprisonment up to life and confiscation for especially large amounts). The trade-finance documentation used to substantiate VAT refunds is also subject to anti-money-laundering and SAFE foreign-exchange scrutiny. Taiwan: false export zero-rating or refund claims cause recapture of tax, late-payment interest, statutory fines (including penalties up to multiple times the tax involved where evasion is established), and criminal prosecution for tax evasion under the Taiwan Tax Evasion and Penalty framework; cross-border supporting records are additionally subject to joint audit and information exchange.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), together with the People's Bank of China for monetary, payment-system, and capital-account settlement matters. Commercial banks act as designated foreign-exchange banks and conduct transaction-level authenticity and compliance reviews.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The renminbi is generally convertible for bona fide current-account transactions, including eligible trade payments, service payments, and profit distributions, subject to bank review, supporting documents, tax compliance, customs or trade data, and applicable foreign-exchange reporting. Capital-account transactions, including foreign-invested enterprise capital contributions, outbound investments, debt financing, guarantees, and certain intercompany flows, remain regulated and may require registration, quota, filing, bank review, or SAFE approval. A WFOE may normally convert distributable after-tax profits and remittance amounts, but must first complete statutory audit and tax settlement, satisfy withholding-tax obligations, document board or shareholder approval, and establish that the remittance is not an unauthorized capital withdrawal or disguised related-party payment. Cross-border transactions involving Taiwan-related counterparties may receive enhanced bank, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, commercial-substance, and cross-Strait regulatory scrutiny.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no general PRC rule requiring ordinary enterprises to mandatorily convert a fixed percentage of export proceeds or surrender all export foreign exchange within a universal statutory period. Eligible export proceeds may generally be retained in a foreign-exchange current account or converted at the enterprise's discretion, subject to SAFE rules, bank verification, customs and trade-data consistency, and enterprise foreign-exchange classification. Banks may require export declarations, commercial contracts, invoices, shipping documents, customs records, collection evidence, and transaction-purpose information. Enterprises classified as Category B or C may face enhanced review, restricted settlement procedures, or additional documentation. Export proceeds used for factoring, reverse factoring, or related-party settlement must remain traceable to the underlying trade and must not be used to disguise capital-account inflows, unauthorized lending, or circular funds. The applicable bank should confirm current SAFE implementation rules and any transaction-specific reporting or settlement deadline before execution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. An offshore electronic-money institution cannot ordinarily replace a PRC domestic bank for a WFOE's RMB basic account, capital account, foreign-exchange settlement account, statutory tax payments, payroll, or regulated factoring collections. Offshore EMI wallets may support limited vendor or customer payments only where the provider is licensed for the relevant corridor and the transaction is processed through lawful cross-border payment arrangements. The WFOE must not use an offshore wallet to bypass SAFE registration, bank authenticity review, capital-account restrictions, foreign-exchange reporting, beneficial-ownership checks, or PRC payment licensing requirements. Taiwan-related wallet and payment arrangements require separate review of cross-Strait restrictions and the provider's authorization in both relevant jurisdictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is not uniformly prohibited, but it is discretionary and commonly limited to preliminary review or selected existing-bank customers. The opening bank will generally require verification of the legal representative, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, directors or controlling persons, business premises, company seals, source of funds, business model, and expected transaction flows. For a newly established WFOE engaged in trade finance or factoring, at least one in-person branch meeting, site visit, or face-to-face video interview is likely. Physical attendance by every director is not universally mandatory, but the legal representative, principal authorized person, or controlling individual may be required to attend. The bank may refuse remote onboarding where identity documents, ownership chains, Taiwan-related counterparties, offshore funding, high-volume receivables, or business substance cannot be independently verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or layered ownership involving offshore companies, nominee shareholders, trusts, or Taiwan-related entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts for every ownership layer; constitutional documents; ownership and control chart to the natural-person UBO; passports and residential evidence; director and shareholder resolutions; notarized or legalized documents where required; explanation of Taiwan-related ownership and control; sanctions and politically exposed person screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Factoring activity appears to constitute unlicensed lending, deposit-taking, payment services, or banking business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business-license scope; commercial-factoring registration or filing evidence where applicable; legal memorandum describing the factoring model; sample receivables-purchase agreements; credit policy; evidence that funding is proprietary or lawfully sourced; prohibition on accepting repayable public deposits; collection and servicing procedures; regulatory correspondence; management biographies demonstrating relevant experience.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear distinction between genuine trade receivables and circular, fictitious, related-party, or self-generated invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying sales contracts; purchase orders; tax invoices; customs declarations; bills of lading; warehouse and delivery confirmations; buyer acknowledgements; account-ledger reconciliations; debtor confirmations; assignment notices; independent credit checks; related-party disclosure; anti-fraud controls; sample transaction audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large or rapid foreign-exchange inflows described as capital, loans, factoring proceeds, or export receipts without consistent purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital contribution certificate or FDI registration evidence; shareholder funding resolution; bank remittance advice; source-of-funds evidence; intercompany loan agreement and registration evidence where required; SAFE and bank forms; contracts, invoices, customs records, and receivables schedules; transaction-purpose matrix mapping each inflow to the applicable SAFE category.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business plan projects unusually high transaction volume, pass-through flows, cash-equivalent activity, or rapid movement between jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury policy; 12-to-24-month cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier concentration analysis; expected monthly turnover; payment-flow diagram; segregation of operating, collection, escrow, and capital accounts; transaction-monitoring thresholds; suspicious-activity escalation procedures; explanation of seasonality and settlement cycles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export or import documentation does not reconcile with customs, tax, logistics, or foreign-exchange records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customs declarations; shipping documents; commercial invoices; packing lists; tax filings; VAT records; logistics-provider confirmations; export proceeds reconciliation; bank statements; exception explanations; corrected declarations; independent accountant certification where discrepancies are material.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary, debtor, supplier, or intermediary is located in a sanctioned, restricted, high-risk, or heavily regulated jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty registry records; beneficial-owner identification; sanctions and adverse-media screening; end-use and end-user certificates; contractual sanctions clauses; payment-chain analysis; country-risk assessment; documented senior-management approval; evidence that no prohibited person or restricted activity is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore accounts, offshore EMIs, personal accounts, virtual assets, cash settlement, or third-party payment instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written rationale; provider licenses; account ownership evidence; service agreements; payment-chain mapping; third-party payment authorization; reconciliations to invoices and contracts; prohibition on personal or unlicensed accounts; enhanced source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; bank pre-clearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient PRC operating substance for a WFOE carrying on regulated or enhanced-risk factoring activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease and site-visit evidence; employee roster; employment contracts; payroll and social-insurance records; local management structure; accounting books; tax registrations; IT and data-security controls; credit-approval committee minutes; servicing resources; documented decision-making performed in the PRC.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder capital through the WFOE's designated foreign-invested enterprise capital account or other bank-approved capital-account structure, using the investor's account in its own name and the correct bank purpose code. Before remittance, complete the applicable market-regulation, foreign-investment information-reporting, and bank or SAFE registration procedures. Provide the capital contribution resolution, investment agreement, ownership documents, remittance instruction, source-of-funds evidence, and registration or filing records. The receiving bank should validate investor identity, amount, currency, registered or subscribed capital terms, beneficial ownership, and purpose before permitting settlement. Convert or use funds only for permitted business purposes; retain supporting vouchers for each payment. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated group companies, offshore EMIs, customer collection accounts, or a trade account in order to avoid capital-account controls. Where shareholder loans are used instead of equity, confirm foreign-debt quota or registration, cross-border financing parameters, interest withholding-tax treatment, transfer-pricing support, and applicable SAFE or bank filing before drawdown.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use domestic RMB clearing through the China National Advanced Payment System or the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) where appropriate, and use a licensed bank's SWIFT foreign-currency channel for international settlements. A SWIFT MT103 should identify the ordering customer, beneficiary, beneficiary bank, amount, currency, invoice or contract reference, purpose, and intermediary-bank information. For documentary trade, use a commercial letter of credit issued or advised through licensed banks under the agreed rules, ordinarily UCP 600, with compliant commercial invoices, transport documents, insurance documents, certificates of origin, inspection records, and other required documents. For open-account purchases, provide the underlying contract, invoice, customs or logistics evidence, and trade-purpose explanation. Factoring collections and disbursements should use dedicated collection accounts or bank-controlled escrow arrangements, with assignment notices, debtor verification, payment instructions, and reconciliation of principal, discount, fees, taxes, and reserves. Banks may apply enhanced review to advance payments, third-party payments, unusual payment chains, related-party settlements, split invoices, and counterparties in Taiwan or other higher-risk corridors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a licensed PRC bank for genuine underlying trade, receivable, payable, or approved financing exposure, supported by documented notional amount, currency, tenor, and exposure evidence.

Non-deliverable forwards only where the executing institution and transaction structure are permitted under current PRC foreign-exchange rules and the instrument is used for a genuine, documented exposure rather than speculation.

Currency swaps or cross-currency swaps arranged with a qualified bank for identifiable funding or currency mismatches, subject to bank credit approval, suitability assessment, accounting treatment, and applicable cross-border financing rules.

Foreign-exchange options or option combinations only through an authorized bank and within applicable product, suitability, margin, and genuine-hedging requirements; speculative or naked derivatives should be prohibited by treasury policy.

Structured trade-linked hedges documented against specific receivable and payable portfolios, with hedge-accounting records, counterparty limits, collateral terms, valuation controls, and board-approved delegation of authority.

No derivative should be entered into solely to generate trading profit, recycle capital, evade settlement restrictions, or create an artificial export or import transaction. The WFOE should maintain hedge registers, exposure reconciliations, mark-to-market records, counterparty confirmations, independent valuation, and evidence of timely close-out or rollover.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Information Declaration (main shareholders and substantial beneficial owner register) under Company Act Art. 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Company Registration and Shareholder Information Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for the preceding fiscal year; any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be filed within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing incurs an administrative fine from NT$50,000 to NT$500,000; false declaration incurs a fine from NT$500,000 to NT$5,000,000; persistent default is recorded as registry non-compliance and may trigger MOEA compulsory deregistration proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (jurisdiction of the WFOE's registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year filers: May 1 – May 31 (no standard extension for private limited companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed filing attracts monthly late-filing surcharge on assessed tax, late-payment interest, and possible estimated assessment; unpaid tax is referred for compulsory attachment; chronic non-filing can lead to a MOEA dissolution order under Company Act Art. 10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Operation Report for Foreign-Invested Enterprise (WFOE foreign-investment status confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 for the preceding calendar year, or the date set by the MOEAIC annual survey circular
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission without good cause may lead to administrative sanction, suspension of foreign-investment incentive privileges, or revocation of the WFOE's investment approval and company registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) – approval of annual financial statements and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders (internal corporate act); approved minutes are entered into the company's registry dossier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must convene within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene exposes the responsible director or officer to an administrative fine of approximately NT$20,000–NT$500,000; any shareholder may petition MOEA to convene the meeting at company cost; repeated default supports a MOEA compulsory dissolution order

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of AGM-approved audited financial statements with the company registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA – Department of Commerce (company registration office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after approval by the shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine imposed on the representative director; non-filing is recorded against the company's registration dossier and, if persistent across consecutive years, triggers registry strike-off risk under Company Act Art. 10

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA-audited financial statements where paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (Company Act Art. 20 and the MOEA threshold order) or where the factoring entity is licensed or regulated by the FSC; due to cross-border factoring and IFRS 9 impairment modeling, an independent audit is commercially required by foreign investors
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Accounting Standards (ROC GAAP) for non-public companies, or International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed by the FSC; cross-border factoring revenue and expected credit loss provisioning follow IFRS 9 and IFRS 15 recognition rules

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Art. 22-1, the WFOE must annually confirm its directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding over 10% of capital by March 31; any shareholding transfer changing the ownership structure must be re-filed within 15 days of the change; the register serves as the AML/KYC baseline for factoring counterparty review
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder ledger and capital contribution schedule)
Minute Book (shareholders' meeting and board meeting minutes)
Substantial beneficial owner and main shareholder information register
